key: But they that wait for the LORD shall renew their strength; They shall mount up with wings as eagles; They shall run, and not be weary; They shall walk, and not faint.
s: The chapter that sets the unwearied Creator against youths who faint and fall closes on this verse; Ibn Ezra, on 40:31, reads the renewal as fresh strength sent by God before the first is spent.

evidence.gloss: ‘They that wait for the LORD shall renew’: before the first strength is spent, another strength comes to them from God; compare ‘if it be cut down, it will sprout again’ (Job 14:7).

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Isaiah 40:31, at [373,31]). Plain sense faithful: 40:28 sets the Creator who ‘fainteth not, neither is weary’ against 40:30’s youths who faint and fall, and 40:31 is the chapter’s last verse; no four-word run from the key. Ibn Ezra on 40:31 (lemma וקוי יי יחליפו) says before the first strength is spent another comes to them from God, which is the reading exactly. He adds a second sense on the whole verse (Israel strengthened and brought back to Jerusalem, Babylon weakened), which does not contradict it; Radak and Metzudat David run close (new strength at every time).
